correctness.rationale: In the centered regular simplex, orthogonal projection to facet j sends barycentric coordinate lambda_j to zero and adds lambda_j/d to every other coefficient; its displacement is proportional to lambda_j. This preserves the strict rank of the unselected coordinates and cycles the face labels. Sorted adjacent gaps obey a row-stochastic primitive companion matrix, whose unique normalized Perron vector gives equally spaced limiting coefficients and exponential convergence. Explicit cyclic points prove existence, rank rotation proves completeness and period d+1, equal positive ties give finite-time arrest, and symmetric facet chambers prove basin size 1/d!. 138033 exact-rational tests from the actual standalone script corroborate dimensions 3-7 but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The 2020/2021 originating paper specifically asks how farthest-facet projections behave on higher-dimensional polytopes. Regular simplices are canonical higher-dimensional test objects, and the claim completely classifies their d! attracting prime-(d+1) cycles, exact barycentric geometry, physical-basin masses and quantitative relaxation. This is a motivated all-dimensional structure theorem, neither a relabeling of the 2D results nor a tiny numerical adjustment.
